findings.summary: .NET Compiler Platform, codenamed Roslyn, is a Microsoft open-source project providing compilers and APIs for C# and Visual Basic. It exposes compilation phases—lexical, syntactic, semantic analysis, and code emission—as reusable services. The compilers are self-hosting, written in C# and VB.NET, and available via NuGet packages. Roslyn enables programmatic compilation, code analysis, and refactoring within IDEs and custom tools.

mechanisms.title: Compiler APIs
mechanisms.explanation: Roslyn exposes APIs that allow direct invocation of compilation phases such as syntax tree construction, semantic binding, and IL code emission. These APIs are accessible from .NET code and support programmatic compilation and analysis.

mechanisms.title: Self-hosting compilers
mechanisms.explanation: The C# and VB.NET compilers within Roslyn are written in their respective languages, enabling the compilers to compile their own source code. This design supports iterative development and tooling built on the platform.
